A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dual-firewall research. Their text, figures, tables, algorithms and complete appendices are readable, and material relocated between the main text and appendices can be matched.

before.justification: v6 reports original firewall evaluations on ConVerse, including privacy, security, utility, component ablations and generalization across personas.

after.justification: v7 retains those empirical results and adds rule-learning sensitivity experiments, an adapted-AirGapAgent comparison and a manual analysis of residual failures.

M1.justification: The dual-firewall procedure, verification, anonymization and rule-learning mechanisms remain unchanged. All five algorithms are retained in Appendices B and E; expanded explanations and experimental rule-data variations do not introduce a new proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ConVerse's travel planning, insurance and real estate domains with the same persona coverage and privacy/security tasks. The added experiments use subsets of this coverage; newly discussed threats are not new evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: v6 cites AirGapAgent but evaluates only unprotected and own-component comparison configurations. v7 Section 5.7 and Table 7 introduce an implemented AirGapAgent adaptation, adding a direct comparison against the closest prior defense using GPT-5 and Travel Planning personas 1 and 4.

E3.justification: The original evaluation settings are retained. New protocols regenerate rules using one persona or one-quarter of the demonstration data and evaluate 24 existing Travel Planning attacks; the AirGapAgent comparison uses all attacks for personas 1 and 4 with upfront relevance filtering.

E4.justification: v7 adds a demonstration-data sensitivity study in Section 5.6 and a manual audit of all residual failures underlying the travel and all-domain results in Section 5.8.1. These substantially extend the retained component ablations, persona generalization and successful qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Existing results retain 95% Wilson intervals for ASR and t-distribution intervals for utility. New Tables 6 and 7 instead report point estimates without confidence intervals or repeated-run details, making uncertainty reporting less consistent.

E6.justification: The original benchmark, ablation and persona-generalization table values are unchanged. New results include reduced-demonstration ASRs of 0–8.3% and, in Table 7's separate comparison, overall privacy ASRs of 67.3% for adapted AirGapAgent versus 5.5% for the dual firewall. New qualitative findings identify residual privacy and security failure patterns.

T1.justification: The formal problem setup, structured-language definition L=(K,V,T) and structural properties are retained. The trusted-knowledge-base assumption moves to Section 6. New scope and mechanism discussions are qualitative, without new formal propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: dual structural firewalls, demonstration-derived domain rules and strong privacy/security reductions while preserving utility. Added experiments support existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v7 replaces tentative residual-privacy explanations with granularity-calibration and field-overlap findings, and distinguishes valid-protocol upselling from assistant-side security errors. Section 6 adds substantive limitations concerning fabricated values, joint re-identification, unstructured domains and noisy demonstrations. The different rule-learning corpora also receive a new mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: v7 adds per-turn call/context information, a verifier-runtime statement and explicit descriptions of released transcripts, learned rules and evaluation resources. Conversely, it omits v6's explicit attribution of unprotected baseline scores to ConVerse and its judge-parsing retry detail; this does not establish changed execution.

R1.justification: v7 adds supporting literature on fraud, reputation, re-identification and privacy preferences, and revises agent-skills references. The central positioning against binary minimization and model-level defenses remains stable. Publication and title updates to retained works are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: v7 extensively condenses the introduction, related work and qualitative exposition, reorganizes the abstraction-method subsections, summarizes benchmark details in the main text and rebuilds Section 6 around discussion and limitations. Appendices A–I reorganize substantial retained technical material.

P2.justification: v7 adds Tables 6–7 and relocates Figure 2, all five algorithm displays and the three original specification tables into appendices. The diagrams and retained table contents remain substantially unchanged, but systematic relocation and regrouping materially alter the document's visual organization.

improvement.justification: Compared with v6, the added baseline comparison, sensitivity test and residual-failure audit provide useful supporting evidence, while Section 6 makes important limitations explicit. The net gain is limited by the new experiments' narrow scope and missing uncertainty intervals. The AirGapAgent comparison also evaluates the entire dual firewall, so it does not isolate abstraction's contribution from language conversion.
